description: Prune block-0 pre-attention LayerNorm biases in nearest-neutral order
proposal: Family: scalar pruning. Current retained frontier is 1,672 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 23 prior attempts in this family. The most recent accepted result was attempt-0059, which fixed block-1 pre-FF scale coordinate 12 at 2,118 parameters/99.05%; the most recent failed result was attempt-0061, whose second block-1 pre-FF scale prune scored 54.19% at 2,117 parameters. The current checkpoint's nearest remaining normalization bias to zero is block 0 pre-attention coordinate 3 at magnitude 1.045e-02, slightly below the nearest block-1 pre-attention alternative at 1.108e-02. Hypothesis: after later scalar unions changed the frontier, this isolated residual bias remains dispensable. The helper orders eligible coordinates by current absolute bias, fixes one to zero per micro-trial, and the official runner alone accepts or rolls back. Stop on the first scored discard or error, when no coordinate remains, at 14 micro-trials, or after 20 wall-clock minutes. This is more informative than opening block 1 first because it is the globally least checkpoint perturbation among untested sparse-normalization biases.
summary: One micro-trial attempted block-0 pre-attention bias coordinate 3, but training never started because the helper generated an invalid tuple by omitting a separator before the new coordinate. Outcomes: 0 accepts, 0 scored discards, 1 implementation error, no official verification, and no frontier change. Stop reason: the declared first-error boundary. The syntax defect is reproducible and has been corrected in the helper; architectural capacity remains untested.
